source_caption: Rush Hour (1998) is an action-comedy about an unlikely partnership between a fast-talking LAPD detective and a disciplined Hong Kong inspector who team up to rescue a kidnapped girl. Starring Jackie Chan and Chris Tucker, the film blends martial arts, humor, and buddy-cop chemistry. Directed by Brett Ratner, it became a major hit and spawned a successful franchise.

source_details.title: Rush Hour
source_details.synopsis: Rush Hour is a 1998 American buddy cop action comedy film directed by Brett Ratner from a screenplay by Jim Kouf and Ross LaManna and a story by LaManna. It stars Jackie Chan, Chris Tucker, Tom Wilkinson, Chris Penn, and Elizabeth Peña. In the film, Hong Kong Police Force (HKPF) Chief Inspector Lee (Chan) and Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) Detective James Carter (Tucker) are forced to work together to rescue a Chinese diplomat's abducted daughter. Development on Rush Hour began in 1995, after LaManna wrote a spec script, which was first initially sold to Hollywood Pictures with Ratner and Chan both attached to the project.
